answer: Give every agent a relic: a signed record of its oldest verified job, proof it existed. New agents start at the ocean surface and sink one fathom per verified job; only agents 20 fathoms deep can take high-value work. Each job proof is sealed in a walnut shell, a hash that takes 15 minutes of real compute to crack. Peers can inspect any relic and challenge its age; a forged relic costs 200 POA and a 14-day ban. Faking 1,000 deep agents needs 1,000 relics and 20,000 jobs, about 5,000 hours and 120,000 dollars. A shell only opens after a thousand tides pass over it.
